title: Coherent cocartesian incidence sections with a fixed source simplex
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, mapping spaces and initial objects of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], trivial Kan fibrations of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $C,J$ be small ordinary categories such that no two nonidentity arrows of $J$ are composable. Let $p:E\to N(C)$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, $d\geq0$, $\tau:\Delta^d\to E$, and $g:\Delta^d\star N(J)\to N(C)$ restricting to $p\tau$. Put $x=\tau(d)$ and let $g_0=g|_{\{d\}\star N(J)}$. For every object $a\in J$, let $f_a:p(x)\to g(a)$ be the corresponding cross edge of $g_0$, and suppose a $p$-cocartesian lift $s_a:x\to y_a$ of $f_a$ is specified.

For each $k$, let $L_k$ consist of pairs $(\sigma,h)$ with $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(J)$ and $h:\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to E$ restricting to $\tau$ and satisfying $ph=g\circ(\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d}\star\sigma)$; use last-block restriction as the simplicial operators. Define $L^0$ similarly with $\{d\}$, $x$ and $g_0$ in place of $\Delta^d$, $\tau$ and $g$. Write $\rho:L\to N(J)$ and $\rho^0:L^0\to N(J)$ for projection. Then $L,L^0$ are quasicategories and last-vertex restriction $R:L\to L^0$ is a trivial Kan fibration over $N(J)$ and a categorical equivalence. For $a\in J$ put $J_a=L\times_{N(J)}\{a\}$ and $J_a^0=L^0\times_{N(J)}\{a\}$. Both are quasicategories; the induced $R_a:J_a\to J_a^0$ is a trivial Kan fibration and a categorical equivalence. Every vertex $z\in J_a$ with $R_a(z)=s_a$ is initial in $J_a$, and such vertices exist.

There is a section $i:N(J)\to L$ with $\rho i=\operatorname{id}$, for which the last edge of the extension $i(a)$ is exactly $s_a$. Its terminal evaluation $N(J)\to E$ carries every arrow of $J$ to a $p$-cocartesian edge. More precisely, any specified vertices $z_a\in J_a$ with $R_a(z_a)=s_a$ can be retained as the vertices of such a section. All of $\tau$, including its earlier vertices and higher faces, stays fixed. These assertions include $d=0$ and $J=\varnothing$.
